answer: Every epoch, each identity must prove physical dispersion by latency triangulation: a quorum of beacons scattered like a nebula across continents fires simultaneous cryptographic pings, and the node must answer all within a window tighter than light-speed round-trips allow. One server pretending to be a harbor of many identities cannot beat physics — its replies to distant beacons arrive late and the cluster is flagged. So N fake identities cost N real machines near N regions: linear, honest, unforgiving, enforced in the kernel of the protocol.
